newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Europe feeds nervous, Brazil strike fuels Chicago.
newsitem.headline: Europe feeds nervous, Brazil strike fuels Chicago.

text.p: European meals and feeds were active and firmed throughout the day, reacting to a sharp rise in Chicago futures where concerns over rain and then a potential port strike in Brazil pushed prices higher.
Dealers said the nearby market in Europe was particularly active for a Monday with consumers buying in cover.

Sellers started offering South American soymeal pellets between $7.00 and $13.00 higher this morning in anticipation of a jump in futures this afternoon. The CBOT soy complex surged at the opening as union officials in Brazil said workers at the Parangua port would strike on Wednesday over a wage claim.

"The market is very nervous and although it was busy for a Monday, it was all concentrated in nearby business. But we should see prices hold overnight and an increase in trading volume tomorrow," one European trader said.

Traders in Brazil said the Parangua port was operating normally on Monday, rejecting a union claim that workers were already loading on a reduced basis. The union has said other ports in the country would join the action at Parangua from Thursday out of sympathy.
